references.text: Another Sabbath incident where a man with a withered hand stood before Jesus. In both cases, the religious leaders watched to see if Jesus would heal on the Sabbath ([ref:Luk 6:6|Luke 6:6]).
Just before this event, Jesus healed a woman with a bent back on the Sabbath, sparking debate with the synagogue leader. Here too, a sick person was "before him" ([ref:Luk 13:11-12|Luke 13:11-12]).
Jesus asks whether it is lawful to heal on the Sabbath and then heals the man with dropsy – the direct continuation of the event in verse 2 ([ref:Luk 14:3-4|Luke 14:3-4]).
Parallel healing situation: In the synagogue there was a man with a withered hand, and the Pharisees watched to see if Jesus would heal him on the Sabbath ([ref:Mark 3:1-2|Mark 3:1-2]).
Here too, a man with a withered hand is present, and they ask Jesus whether it is lawful to heal on the Sabbath – a situation very similar to that in Luke 14:2 ([ref:Matt 12:10|Matthew 12:10]).

A man who had been sick for thirty-eight years was healed by Jesus – yet another example of Jesus seeking out and healing a chronically ill person, followed by Sabbath controversy ([ref:Joh 5:5-6|John 5:5-6]).

Jesus sees a man born blind and heals him on the Sabbath, once again raising the question of healing on the Sabbath. The pattern of a sick person standing "before" Jesus and sparking controversy repeats itself ([ref:Joh 9:1-2|John 9:1-2]).
